name: Chapter 60-01. Deposits - General Provisions
scope: chapter N.D. Cent. Code ch. 60-01 (North Dakota Legislative Branch, the whole code on one page)

notice.label: Notice before it is used on a person
notice.quote: In the absence of an agreement as to the length of time during which a deposit is to continue, it may be terminated by the depositor at any time and by the depositary upon reasonable notice.

hearing.label: A chance to answer before the decision is final

appeal.label: A way to a court or an independent reviewer

access.label: The person can see the record

standing.label: The person can enforce it themselves

self-report.label: The law must report its own effects

waiver.label: Who can waive it; does it expire

symmetry.label: Binds individuals harder than institutions
symmetry.qe: No hotelkeeper who constantly has in the hotelkeeper's inn or hotel a metal safe or suitable vault in good order and fit for the custody of money, bank notes, jewelry, articles of gold and silver manufacture, precious stones, personal ornaments, railroad mileage books or tickets,

boundary.label: What it takes from you, and the limits on that
boundary.quote_limits: A depositary may not use the thing deposited nor permit it to be used for any purpose without the consent of the depositor.

plain-words.label: Can an ordinary reader follow it
plain-words.quote_longest: No hotelkeeper who constantly has in the hotelkeeper's inn or hotel a metal safe or suitable vault in good order and fit for the custody of money, bank notes, jewelry, articles of gold and silver manufacture, precious stones, personal ornaments, railroad mileage books or tickets,

fair-exchange.label: What a person gives, and what a person gets
fair-exchange.quote_gives: If a thing deposited with a depositary is damaged by the wrongful use thereof by the depositary, the depositary is liable for such damage unless such damage inevitably must have happened though the property had not been used in that manner.
fair-exchange.quote_gets: An involuntary deposit is gratuitous, the depositary being entitled to no reward.
